subject: Reserve commitment ladder — staggered prepay proposal and questions
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acmeai.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>; David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserve commitment: proposed staggered ladder for Dedicated GPUs

Hannah / David —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As discussed, Acme AI is evaluating a multi-year reserve for Dedicated capacity to support our customer-facing agents and internal embedding pipelines. We want to propose a staggered/prepay ladder so we can align spend with expected product launches next year. High-level ask:

- Year 1 (first 12 months): start with 18 GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent) + 1 TPM pool for embeddings;
- Months 7–12: ramp to 36 GPUs (burst-capable up to 48) as we onboard a new product;
- Year 2: target 72 GPUs steady state; Year 3: 96 GPUs (contingent on adoption)

We're open to a 2–3 year commitment with annual prepay tranches. Key constraints for us: predictable unit price, ability to shift credits if adoption lags, and a clearly defined ramp schedule that lets us get staged discounts for earlier prepay.

Attached is a consolidated requirements spreadsheet (Acme_Ramp_Requirements_v2.xlsx) with timing windows, critical dates, and expected token throughput. Can you/your pricing team provide 1) an annual prepay option (year-by-year invoices/credits) with stepped discounts tied to committed GPUs and 2) a multi-year prepay with a larger term discount but explicit credit conversion rules if we under-deploy? Also want to understand whether Redwood supports limited burst capacity on Dedicated pools (guaranteed baseline vs. burstable headroom) and any onboarding credits for the first 30 days.

Appreciate any initial sketches by end of week — we need this for our Q4 planning sync.

Best,
Sarah Jones
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme AI

Subject: Re: Reserve commitment: proposed staggered ladder for Dedicated GPUs

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear requirements sheet and timeline. Looping in David and Lauren for commercial pricing and Vivek for coverage on term exceptions. A few clarifying items before we put numbers on paper:

- Can you confirm whether the burst headroom (e.g., 48 GPUs in Months 7–12) must be reserved capacity or if you are OK with a mix of reserved baseline + guaranteed burst pool (we can define a burst SLA but discounts differ).
- For TPM (embeddings) pools, do you expect steady usage or a seasonal spike pattern tied to product launches? The elasticity profile affects suggested batch/quantization knobs we recommend.
- When you say "convert credits" if under-deployed, do you mean a roll-forward of unused prepaid credit to future tranches, or a partial refund? We typically recommend roll-forward credits with a timebox (12 months) to preserve committed economics.

I'll put together two sketches: (A) annual prepay ladder with modest term discount + convertible rolling credits, and (B) multi-year prepay with larger term discount but stricter non-refundable tranches and a defined staircase ramp. Expect the PDF with a sample ramp and rough pricing tomorrow. If you're free, can we schedule a 30-minute call Thursday to walk options?

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserve commitment: proposed staggered ladder for Dedicated GPUs

Sarah / team —

Appreciate the detail — attached is a quick pricing breakdown with two alternative structures (RDW_option_pricing_breakdown_20260811.csv). Summary here:

Option 1 — 3-year prepaid (higher term discount):
- Year 1 prepaid: 24 GPUs baseline, ramp to 36 by month 12; Year 2 prepaid 72 GPUs; Year 3 prepaid 96 GPUs
- Term discount: 15% off list Dedicated unit rates (applies to prepaid portion)
- Credit policy: prepaid dollars apply to capacity; unused credits roll forward up to 12 months and then convert to a one-time service credit (no refunds)
- Burst policy: guaranteed baseline + 25% burst pool (subject to capacity windowing); SLA-backed latency floor for baseline
- Onboarding: 30-day technical assistance credit (equivalent to 1 GPU week)

Option 2 — Annual prepay (more flexibility):
- Yearly commitments with annual prepay invoiced each year; ramp gates mid-year
- Discount: 8% on year-by-year prepay; discretionary early-payment credit for Q1 prepay
- Credit policy: unused credits can be reallocated within the same 12-month year but do not roll across contract years without an amendment

A few commercial notes:
- We can offer a limited convertible clause (move unused prepaid credits between GPU and TPM buckets) but that requires explicit mapping in the SOW and impacts the discount slope.
- For aggressive burst needs, we can provision burst credits as a billable addon or reserve a steady-state headroom at higher unit price.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether Acme prefers refund-like flexibility (we typically avoid refunds) vs. roll-forward credits;
2) Choose Option 1 (term-forward economics) or Option 2 (annual flexibility) — we will then produce a legal-ready SOW and DocuSign envelope;
3) If you want a short proof-of-concept warm-up, we can spin a dedicated warm pool for 30 days under a trial addendum.

If that sounds good I'll ask Legal to prepare a starter SOW with convertible-credit language and a proposed DocuSign link. Happy to jump on the Thursday call Hannah suggested — I'm available 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

David / Hannah —

Thanks for the clear options — helpful and exactly the level we needed. A few quick clarifications before we proceed to SOW:

- We prefer roll-forward credits (not refunds) but need a 24-month roll-forward window for Year 1 prepaid dollars (our adoption window may be longer). Would Redwood be able to extend roll-forward to 24 months for Year 1, with step-down to 12 months thereafter?
- For convertible credits between GPU and TPM buckets: can you include a simple conversion rate in the SOW (e.g., X TPU-equivalent tokens = 1 GPU-credit) so our finance team can forecast?
- We would like a limited 30-day warm pool trial. Can that be included as a trial addendum with a target provisioning SLA?

If you can update Option 1 to show a variant with 24-month roll-forward on Year 1 prepaid dollars and include the conversion metric, we can route to Legal and Procurement. Please attach the DocuSign envelope for the SOW draft when ready — procurement is standing by.

Thanks,
Sarah Jones
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme AI
